item.name: UAT - Full User Flow (Owner -> Manager -> Staff)
item.description: Run top-to-bottom with Postman's Collection Runner (or Ctrl/Cmd+Enter through each request in order) against a clean environment. Each step auto-saves the IDs/tokens the next one needs via a Test script - no manual copy/pasting required, except CreateProduct's image file (Postman can't attach a local file from a saved collection without you picking it once). Mirrors docs/WORKFLOWS.md Sections 3-5 (Owner/Manager/Staff Journeys): tenant provisioning, owner setup (staff/catalog/procurement), a cashier's full shift (open -> void with manager approval -> a cash+QR split sale -> close), a manager-approved return after the shift closes, then owner back-office oversight (reports + audit log).

request.description: Step 1 of the UAT flow. Creates a fresh Organization + Owner + Service Center login. Saves the new org's id for every following request.
Attaches the login this register's staff will use in Stage 2. No id needs saving - the email/password are already fixed literals this folder reuses.
Owner session for every Stage 1 setup call below. Auto-saves {{token}}/{{refreshToken}} (same script as the regular Login request).
role 3 = manager (see GET /roles). pin is Manager Mia's own PIN, used later for VerifyManagerPIN approvals.
role 1 = staff (cashier). This is who rings the sales in Stage 2.

MANUAL STEP: a product needs a real image and Postman can't ship a local file inside an exported collection - click the "image" field below and pick any picture once before running this request (the Collection Runner will then reuse whatever you picked). Everything else is already filled in and chained.
Sets the product's weighted-average cost basis once received below, so Stage 4's GetProfitAndLoss has a real, non-zero COGS.
CreatePurchaseOrder's response doesn't include each item's own id - fetch it here so the goods receipt below can reference it.
Stocks the product (20 units) and blends its cost basis via weighted-average (0 -> 300.00, since there was no prior stock).

Switches {{token}} from the Owner's org-wide session to this register's branch-bound session - everything from here through Stage 3 needs a branch-bound token (org_id AND branch_id both come from it, never the request body).
A throwaway sale, rung up wrong on purpose so the next two steps can demonstrate a manager-approved void.
Restores Sale A's stock and excludes it from the shift's cash reconciliation (only completed sales count).
The real sale that stays on the books - 3 units, split cash+QR (the only 2 accepted payment methods this version). Kept for Stage 3's return and Stage 4's reports.
Expected cash = opening 100 + Sale B's cash portion 1000 (Sale A doesn't count - it was voided, not completed). closing_cash matches exactly, so no reason is required.

item.name: 3.1 GetSaleReceipt (Sale B, to read its sale_item id)

request.description: CreateSale's response doesn't include each line's own id - fetch it here so the return below can reference it.

item.name: 3.3 CreateReturn (1 of the 3 units, customer changed mind)

request.description: Can happen any time after a completed sale (no shift-open requirement, unlike Void) - restocks the 1 returned unit since condition is sellable.

item.name: 4.1 Login as Owner (to see org-wide back office)

request.description: Switches {{token}} back to the Owner's org-wide session for the reports/audit calls below.
Should show Sale B's 1500 gross, the 1 returned unit, cash+QR split, and Instant Noodles as the top product - Sale A doesn't appear anywhere, it was voided.
Net Sales minus COGS (3 units sold @ cost 300, less the 1 returned unit's cost) minus Expenses (0, none logged) = Net Profit. Adjust from/to if you run this outside October 2026.
Should show the manager-approved void and the manager-approved return, newest first.

Shagan-team-only. Protected by X-Internal-Key (INTERNAL_API_KEY), not the regular bearer token - creates Organization + owner User + service_center User in one call. No Branch is created here; use POST /branches (as the owner) afterward, then POST /devices, then POST /internal/accounts/pos to attach a pos-type login to a device.

Shagan-team-only. Protected by X-Internal-Key (INTERNAL_API_KEY). Attaches a new pos-type User to an existing Organization + Device - device_id must already belong to org_id, otherwise returns 404 (not 403 - same not-found-not-forbidden reasoning as branches/staff/devices).

Shagan-team-only. Protected by X-Internal-Key (INTERNAL_API_KEY). Creates a Branch for org_id without needing an authenticated owner session - used right after CreateAccount, before the owner has ever logged in. Same validation/logic as the authenticated POST /branches, just with an explicit org_id instead of one read from the JWT.

Shagan-team-only. Protected by X-Internal-Key (INTERNAL_API_KEY). Registers a Device on branch_id without needing an authenticated owner session - branch_id must already belong to org_id, otherwise returns 404 (not 403 - same not-found-not-forbidden reasoning as the authenticated device/branch endpoints).
Shagan-team-only. Every organization, no filter - there's no tenant JWT to scope this from.

Shagan-team-only. Suspends or reactivates a whole tenant - status is "active" or "suspended". A suspended org blocks Login/RefreshSession for every one of its users (owner, service_center, and pos alike), not just individually-suspended pos accounts.
Shagan-team-only. Reuses the same logic as the tenant-facing GET /branches, with org_id (required query param) instead of a JWT.
Shagan-team-only. Reuses the same logic as the tenant-facing GET /devices, with org_id (required query param) instead of a JWT.
Shagan-team-only. Every pos-type login in the given org (required query param).

Shagan-team-only. Suspends or reactivates a single pos-terminal login, independent of the underlying Device's own status - status is "active" or "suspended". Returns 404 if :id isn't a pos-type account (this endpoint can't be used to disable an owner/service_center login).
Shagan-team-only. Resets a pos-terminal login's password - password is plaintext, hashed server-side before it's persisted. Returns 404 if :id isn't a pos-type account.

Short-lived elevation token for a single approval (void/return/exchange/manual-discount/drawer-without-sale) - NOT for a manager's own backoffice sign-in, use VerifyStaffPIN for that. Requires a valid bearer access token (the calling device or owner) - :id is the staff being asked to approve, scoped to the caller's org (and branch, if the caller's own token carries one). permission is the specific permission code this approval is for (e.g. approve_void, approve_return, approve_exchange, apply_manual_discount, open_drawer_no_sale) - the target staff's role must actually grant it (doesn't have to be role=manager specifically - whichever role has that permission), checked via the same Roles/Permissions matrix as GET /roles/:id/permissions. Wrong staff, wrong branch, wrong PIN, and role-lacks-permission all return the same generic 401 (never 404) - a terminal can't enumerate staff IDs, branches, or role grants by probing. On success, returns the Staff record plus a separate 2-minute token (authtoken.StaffClaims, auto-saved here into {{managerApprovalToken}}) - much shorter than VerifyStaffPIN's 12-hour shift token, since this proves one momentary approval, not a signed-in session. The original cashier's own {{staffToken}} is untouched - pass this approval token separately as X-Manager-Approval-Token on the actual action (e.g. CreateSale, CreateDrawerEvent) alongside the cashier's X-Staff-Token. After 5 consecutive wrong PINs, this staff's PIN locks out for 15 minutes (shared with VerifyManagerPIN/VerifyStaffPIN - same underlying PinHash) - further attempts return 429 with an unlock timestamp, even with the correct PIN.

Cashier PIN sign-on at a terminal. Requires a valid bearer access token (the calling device or owner) - :id is the Staff being verified, scoped to the caller's org. If the caller's own token carries a branch_id (a pos-device token), the staff must belong to that same branch, otherwise this returns the same generic 401 as a wrong PIN (never 404) - a terminal can't be used to enumerate staff IDs or which branch they belong to. An owner/service_center token (no branch_id) can verify any staff in the org. On success, returns the Staff record plus a separate, shift-length staff-session token (12h TTL) - distinct from the caller's own device/owner access token. After 5 consecutive wrong PINs, this staff's PIN locks out for 15 minutes (shared with VerifyManagerPIN/VerifyStaffPIN - same underlying PinHash) - further attempts return 429 with an unlock timestamp, even with the correct PIN.

Lists staff at this branch whose role grants the given permission code (query param, required) - not staff with role=manager specifically, since e.g. apply_manual_discount is granted to both super_staff and manager (see the v1 role/permission grant table). Use this to build a picker of who's eligible to approve a specific action before calling VerifyManagerPIN with the same permission code. An unrecognized permission code just returns an empty list, not an error.

Open shift with opening float. Requires X-Staff-Token (run VerifyStaffPIN first - it auto-saves into {{staffToken}}). The shift always belongs to whichever staff that token identifies - staff_id in the body is ignored even if sent. That same staff member is the only one who can later close it.
GetCurrentShift
GetShift

closing_cash is what the person closing the shift actually counted in the drawer - only cash is physically counted, card/QR/mobile-wallet payments are trusted to match what the system recorded. reason is required only when closing_cash doesn't match the system's expected cash total (opening_cash + cash sales this shift); otherwise 400. Writes one ShiftReconciliation row per payment method as a side effect. Requires X-Staff-Token, and returns 403 unless it identifies the same staff member who opened this shift - run VerifyStaffPIN as that staff first.

Manager-only override of CloseShift's "same staff who opened it" rule - for when that staff is genuinely unavailable (e.g. called in sick) and the till would otherwise stay locked open indefinitely. Requires an X-Staff-Token whose role grants access_backoffice (a Manager), or 403. Unlike a normal close, reason is ALWAYS required here, even if closing_cash matches exactly - the override itself needs justification. The closed shift keeps its original staff_id (whoever opened it) but records closed_by_staff_id as whoever performed this override, so the two can be told apart afterward.

Cash drawer opened, with or without a triggering sale. sale_id is optional and must be a real Sale's UUID (not an integer) when given - e.g. copy the id from a CreateSale response. Requires X-Staff-Token - the event is always attributed to whichever staff that token identifies, not a client-supplied staff_id. Omitting sale_id (opening the drawer with no sale) additionally requires the calling staff's role to grant open_drawer_no_sale (super_staff/manager, per the seeded grants - note manager does NOT have this one by default, only super_staff does) OR a valid X-Manager-Approval-Token granting it instead (enable that header and run VerifyManagerPIN with permission=open_drawer_no_sale first, as a staff member who does have it) - 403 without either. A drawer event tied to a real sale_id needs no such check.
ListDrawerEvents
ListExpenses
Requires X-Staff-Token - always logged as created by whichever staff that token identifies, not a client-supplied created_by.
Requires X-Staff-Token. Returns 403 unless that token identifies either the staff member who originally logged this expense, or someone with access_backoffice (a Manager).
Requires X-Staff-Token. Same authorization as UpdateExpense - only the original creator or a Manager (access_backoffice) may delete it.

Lists products in the caller's org. If the caller's token carries a branch (a pos device), results are restricted to that branch automatically - owner/service_center tokens see every branch. No query params - the scope comes from the token, not something the client can override.

query.description: Required only for an owner/service_center token (no branch on the token). Ignored for a pos-device token, which always uses its own branch.

request.description: Exact-match barcode lookup, scoped to the caller's org and branch - returns the product plus its "images" array (see ListProducts), same presigned-URL/15-minute-TTL reasoning. Barcode is only unique per branch (not per org), so a branch is always required: a pos-device token supplies its own branch automatically; an owner/service_center token must pass ?branch_id= (enable the disabled query param below and set it to a real branch id in that org).
GetProduct

Multipart upload: every product field as a form field, plus "image" (required product photo - attach it yourself, no default file is set). branch_id/category_id must belong to your own org. modifier is optional - leave blank for null.

Multipart upload, scoped to the caller's org (org_id can never be reassigned via this endpoint). Every field is optional - only send what you want to change, remove any row you don't need (an unselected "image" file row causes a Postman bug - EISDIR - so delete it entirely rather than leaving it empty). branch_id/category_id, if sent, must belong to your own org. price/discount/tax are validated against the resulting combined state (existing values fill in for anything not sent), not just the fields in this request. image, if attached, entirely replaces the product's existing photo. modifier can't be cleared back to null via PATCH yet - omitting it just leaves it unchanged. cost_price lets you set the cost basis directly (e.g. for stock never received through a real Procurement goods receipt) - it never appears in GET /products or GET /products/:id (business-sensitive, only readable via GET /reports/profit-loss).

Hard delete, scoped to the caller's org. Blocked with 409 if any combo still bundles this product (create a combo referencing it via CreateCombo to test that path). On success, also removes the product's own image and its storage object - 204 No Content, no body.

Multipart upload: name, price, expires_at (RFC3339), and items (a JSON-encoded array of {"product_id","qty"} objects) as form fields, plus an optional "image" file - unlike CreateProduct, a combo can be created without one (leave the file field empty to skip it). price must be > 0, expires_at must be in the future, and items must have at least one entry with no duplicate product_id - each product_id must already exist in your org (create products first via CreateProduct).

Multipart upload, scoped to the caller's org (org_id can never be reassigned via this endpoint). Every field is optional - only send what you want to change. price/expires_at are validated against the resulting combined state (existing values fill in for anything not sent). To also replace the image, add an "image" file field yourself and attach a real file - do NOT add an empty/unselected file field, since Postman has a bug (EISDIR) where a present-but-empty file field breaks the request; only add the row when you're attaching an actual file. Doesn't support editing items yet - only the combo's own fields and its image.
Hard delete, scoped to the caller's org. Nothing currently blocks this (no Sales/order-history domain yet referencing combos) - also removes the combo's own items and image. 204 No Content, no body.

Lists combos in the caller's org. No query params - org_id comes from the token. Each combo now includes an "images" array (id, url, width, height) - url is a temporary presigned link valid for 15 minutes, so re-fetch the list if it expires.

query.description: Optional - owner/service_center only (a pos-device token's own branch always wins instead). Must belong to your own org.
Optional - narrows to one product.

request.description: Lists stock levels in the caller's org. Restricted to the caller's own branch when the token carries one (a pos device) - org-wide otherwise, same reasoning as ListProducts. Both query params are optional - omit either to leave that dimension unfiltered.

query.description: Optional - owner/service_center only (a pos-device token's own branch always wins instead). Must belong to your own org.

request.description: Lists stock levels that have fallen to or below their product's own reorder threshold. Same scoping as ListStockLevels - restricted to the caller's own branch when the token carries one, org-wide otherwise. branch_id is optional.

query.description: Optional - a pos-device token's own branch always wins instead.
Optional - narrows to one product.

request.description: Read-only audit trail - never written directly by a client. Org-scoped, both query params optional. Ordered oldest-first, since each row's balance_after only reads as a running balance in chronological order.

Applies delta to product_id's stock at its own branch (a product lives at exactly one branch - branch_id is never client-supplied) and writes one inventory_ledger row, atomically. delta can be positive (e.g. a manual recount finding more stock) or negative (e.g. shrinkage/damage). Returns 409 Conflict if delta would take quantity below zero - stock can never go negative from a movement this domain controls. actor_id is never client input - it's the authenticated caller's own user ID. unit_cost is optional and only meaningful alongside a positive delta (you're adding stock, so you can say what it's worth) - when given, it blends into the product's cost basis by weighted average, same method a Procurement goods receipt uses. Rejected (400) if given alongside a zero-or-negative delta, or if negative itself.

query.description: Optional - owner/service_center only (a pos-device token's own branch always wins instead). Matches a transfer where this branch is either the sender or the receiver.

request.description: Lists stock transfers in the caller's org. Same scoping as ListStockLevels. branch_id is optional and matches a transfer where the branch is either from_branch or to_branch.

Creates a new stock transfer at status pending - no stock moves yet. from_branch/to_branch must both belong to your org and differ. Every item's product must belong to your org AND to from_branch specifically (a product lives at exactly one branch). actor_id is never client input - it's the authenticated caller's own user ID. Advance it with UpdateStockTransfer - moving it to completed is what actually decrements from_branch's stock and credits to_branch's.

Advances a stock transfer's status: pending -> in_transit -> completed, or -> cancelled from either pending or in_transit. Rejects with 409 Conflict if the transfer is already completed or cancelled. Moving to completed is the one transition with a real stock effect - decrements every item's qty from from_branch and credits it to to_branch, atomically, writing one transfer_out and one transfer_in inventory_ledger row per item. Rejects with 409 Conflict if from_branch doesn't have enough stock for any item - nothing moves for any item in that case. status must be one of: in_transit, completed, cancelled.

Requires a branch-bound pos-device token (org_id and branch_id both come from it, never the body) AND X-Staff-Token (run VerifyStaffPIN first - it auto-saves into {{staffToken}}). id is a client-generated UUID (idempotency key for the offline-first device). Subtotal/Discount/Tax/Total are NOT accepted at the sale level - each item snapshots its own tax (from Product.Tax, same offline-first reasoning as unit_price/name_snapshot); the server sums Subtotal/Discount/Tax from items and derives Total = Subtotal - Discount + Tax, then rejects the request (400) if payments don't add up to that Total. combo_id is optional - set it to tag several line items as components of the same Combo rung up together (purely a grouping label for receipts/reporting; each component is still priced/taxed/discounted as its own normal line item). shift_id must be a currently-open shift belonging to this branch, else 404. Status/completed_at are always server-set to completed/now(). Any item's discount or tax must be zero or greater (400 otherwise). A positive item discount requires the calling staff's role to grant apply_manual_discount (only super_staff/manager have it by default) OR a valid X-Manager-Approval-Token granting it (enable that header and run VerifyManagerPIN with permission=apply_manual_discount first, as the target staff) - 403 without either. Stock decrement/inventory-ledger writes are deliberately deferred until the Inventory domain exists.
Org-scoped, newest-completed-first.
Org-scoped - returns 404 for a sale that exists but belongs to a different org, same as one that doesn't exist at all.
Structured receipt data (sale + items + payments) - not printer-specific ESC/POS byte formatting, which belongs to Platform's printer integration, not here.
Returns the same bundle as GetSaleReceipt - a receipt's content never changes between its first print and a reprint.
CreateHeldSale
ListHeldSales
Resume - atomic delete-and-restore

Reverses the entire sale - there is no partial void (see docs/WORKFLOWS.md Section 9). Requires X-Staff-Token; the acting staff needs approve_void themselves, OR X-Manager-Approval-Token grants it instead. Rejects (409) if the sale is already voided, if its shift is no longer open (a void is only valid within the same shift it was rung up in), or if any Return/Exchange already references it. Credits back every item's decremented stock and marks the sale voided, atomically.

query.description: Optional - owner/service_center only (a pos-device token's own branch always wins instead).

request.description: Lists voids in the caller's org. Restricted to the caller's own branch when the token carries one - org-wide otherwise, same reasoning as inventory.ListStockLevels.

Also writes return_items. Requires X-Staff-Token; the acting staff needs approve_return themselves, OR X-Manager-Approval-Token grants it instead. Confirms the sale is completed (not voided) and every item belongs to it with enough not-yet-returned-or-exchanged qty remaining, computes refund_total server-side from each item's own original per-unit price (never client-supplied), and restocks each condition="sellable" item at the sale's own branch - all atomically. No fixed return time window in v1 - any completed sale can be returned regardless of age.

query.description: Optional - owner/service_center only (a pos-device token's own branch always wins instead).

request.description: Lists returns in the caller's org. Same scoping as ListVoids.
Same scoping as ListVoids.

Also writes exchange_items. Requires X-Staff-Token; the acting staff needs approve_exchange themselves, OR X-Manager-Approval-Token grants it instead. Modeled as one combined transaction (not a chained Return-then-Sale). An "in" item (sale_item_id) is something the customer is returning - its price is derived from the original sale, never client input. An "out" item (product_id + unit_price) is a new item the customer is taking instead. net_difference is computed server-side (out total minus in total) - positive means the customer owes more, negative means they're owed the difference. Credits stock for "in" items and decrements it for "out" items at the sale's own branch, atomically.

query.description: Optional - owner/service_center only (a pos-device token's own branch always wins instead).

request.description: Lists exchanges in the caller's org. Same scoping as ListVoids.
Same scoping as ListVoids.

query.description: Optional - partial, case-insensitive match on name OR phone

request.description: Org-scoped. search is optional - a case-insensitive partial match against name OR phone in one field, matching a POS lookup screen's single search box. Omit it to list every customer in the caller's org.

Inline creation from the POS cart. org_id is never accepted here - it's taken from the caller's own token. tags is optional. consent_status isn't client-settable either - every new customer starts at "pending"; it only changes via POST /customers/:id/consents, which writes a real CustomerConsent audit row (see that endpoint's description). phone is unique per-org, not globally - the same phone number can exist in two different orgs.
Org-scoped - returns 404 for a customer that exists but belongs to a different org, same as one that doesn't exist at all. Detail only for now - purchase history needs Sales, which doesn't exist yet.
Org-scoped via the customer - returns 404 if :id doesn't belong to the caller's org. The full consent audit trail for this customer, oldest first.

customer_id isn't in the body - it's the :id path param. changed_at isn't client-settable either - the server stamps it at creation, same as Device.LastSeenAt. Writes a real CustomerConsent audit row AND updates the cached customers.consent_status in one atomic transaction - a failure partway through never leaves the cache out of sync with the actual consent history. status is one of: granted, revoked, pending. source is one of: pos, online, sms, email.
Lists suppliers in the caller's org. No query params - org_id comes from the token.

Creates a supplier in the caller's org (org_id comes from the token, never the body). last_order_at isn't client-settable - it's stamped at creation, then later updated whenever a real purchase order is placed with this supplier.
Partial update, scoped to the caller's org. Every field is optional - only send what you want to change. last_order_at can't be changed via this endpoint - it's system-managed.
Hard delete, scoped to the caller's org. Blocked with 409 if any purchase order still references this supplier. 204 No Content, no body.

Lists purchase orders in the caller's org. No query params - org_id comes from the token (resolved via the caller's own suppliers, since PurchaseOrder has no org_id column of its own). Returns bare headers only - no items array (see GetPurchaseOrder for that).

Also writes purchase_order_items. supplier_id and every item's product_id must belong to your own org. total is computed from items (sum of ordered_qty*unit_cost) - don't send it. status/created_by aren't accepted either - a new order always starts at "submitted"; created_by is the authenticated caller's own user ID.
Org-scoped. Unlike ListPurchaseOrders, includes an "items" array (the order's line items) - a detail view needs to show what was ordered.

Status transitions: one of draft, submitted, approved, cancelled - NOT received (409). Marking an order received only happens via CreateGoodsReceipt, which requires an actual reconciled receipt. Blocked with 409 once the order is already received or cancelled (terminal states). supplier_id, if sent, must belong to your own org. total/created_by aren't editable here.

Posting increases stock (by received_qty only - never ordered_qty) + writes one inventory ledger entry per item, then marks the purchase order received. po_item_id must belong to this order. variance_note is required whenever received_qty differs from that item's ordered_qty (the lost/extra amount is recorded there, traceable from the ledger entry - not written as a second phantom ledger row). received_qty of 0 is valid (total loss). Blocked with 409 if this order is already received or cancelled. received_by isn't accepted - it's the authenticated caller's own user ID. total_amount/variance_count aren't accepted either - both are computed from items.

query.description: Optional - omit for the org-wide default. Ignored (uses the caller's own branch) for a pos-device/manager token.

request.description: Returns branch_id's override if one exists, else falls back to the org-wide default.

request.description: Upserts the org-wide default (omit branch_id) or a branch-specific override (set branch_id). OrgID always comes from the token.

query.description: Required for an owner/service_center token. Ignored (uses the caller's own branch) for a pos-device/manager token.

request.description: Pure simulation - no real printer integration. Confirms branch ownership and renders a canned test-receipt payload; nothing is persisted.
Multipart upload: "file" (the QR image) + "bank_name". At most 5 active QR codes per branch, one per bank - delete an existing one to free a slot.
Lists the branch's active QR codes only, each with a temporary signed image URL.
Soft-deletes - sets is_active false and removes the image from storage, freeing a cap slot while keeping the row for history.

query.description: Optional - owner/service_center only (a pos-device token's own branch always wins instead).

request.description: Read-only; written via mutation hooks in other domains' own service methods, not a public POST. Curated v1 scope (not every mutation everywhere): Void/Return/Exchange approvals, manual discount applications, and staff record changes (role/PIN/status). Each entry's before/after are full JSON snapshots (before is null for a Create-shaped action like a Return/Exchange/discount, since nothing existed beforehand). Ordered newest-first.

query.description: Optional - owner/service_center only (a pos-device token's own branch always wins instead).

request.description: Snapshot + ETag for offline caching (products/categories/combos) - everything a device needs cached locally to ring up sales offline. Send the ETag response header back as If-None-Match on a later call - a 304 with no body means the device's cached copy is still current, saving the re-download. The ETag is stable across calls even though each image's URL is a freshly re-signed link every time (it hashes a redacted copy with URLs blanked out, not the raw response).

Batch-uploads a device's offline-queued sales - each shaped exactly like a normal POST /sales body. branch_id comes from the caller's own pos-device token, never client input. Idempotent by each sale's own client-generated id - resubmitting an already-arrived sale is a safe no-op reported as success, not an error. Every queued sale is treated as pre-authorized (manual discounts included, no permission re-check) since it already happened at the register. If it would take a product's stock negative, it's let through anyway (not rejected) and a SyncConflict is recorded instead - see GetSyncStatus/ListSyncConflicts. A sale that fails for another reason (e.g. its shift has since closed) is reported as a failed item in the response, not silently dropped.

query.description: Optional - owner/service_center only (a pos-device token's own branch always wins instead).

request.description: unresolved_conflict_count and last_synced_at (the most recent Sale.SyncedAt among sales in scope, null if none have ever synced - only IngestQueuedSales ever sets it).

query.description: Optional - owner/service_center only (a pos-device token's own branch always wins instead).

request.description: The one real cross-device conflict this domain expects: two offline devices both sold the last unit of something. Each row's payload is the product/branch/resulting (negative) qty - resolve it manually via the Inventory Ledger, then PATCH .../resolve to mark it reviewed.

request.description: A real P&L statement over from/to (default: the last 30 days): Net Sales (same Gross-Discounts-Returns formula as SalesSummary) minus COGS (SUM(SaleItem.UnitCost * Qty), a per-sale snapshot of Product.CostPrice taken at sale time - never client-supplied) equals Gross Profit; minus Expenses (shift.Expense, already real per-branch data) equals Net Profit. COGS is only as reliable as the product's own cost basis - a product that's never been through a real Procurement goods receipt or a manual cost_price edit (see UpdateProduct) reads as cost 0, overstating margin until one happens. Returns naturally reduce COGS too (via ReturnItem's own link back to the original SaleItem), no separate tracking needed.
